No - I don't believe that endangered species should be "protected."

Why?

In part because it's authoritarianism in action, and suffers from all of the faults and failures of authoritarianism - selective regulation and enforcement to further the interests of those who lust for and gain authority and their cronies and patrons, and the waste of enormous amounts of money in corruption and bureaucratic ineptitude.

Mostly though, just because I believe that evolution works.

First, if a species is truly unfit to survive in a particular habitat, then that's just the way it is. Other species will take its place - they always do.

Second, if biological diversity truly is crucial to human survival, then humans who don't pursue it will suffer and humans who do pursue it will thrive, and the human species as a whole will, over time, select for that trait and we'll reach a point at which diversity will be protected on a day-to-day basis. It won't be protected by granting megalomaniacs the authority for which they lust so that they can abuse it for their own advantage and the advantage of their cronies and patrons, all while providing cover for a veritable army of incompetent and overpaid parasites (which is an inefficient method at best), but because the humans who have survived will simply choose, on a day-to-day basis, to live in a way that promotes the biological diversity on which they depend.

In the worst case scenario, if biological diversity is in fact crucial to human survival and if humans do not alter their behavior sufficiently to protect it individually and on a day-to-day basis, then the species as a whole will eliminate itself, and that too will just be the way it goes.

No matter what - no matter the process nor the outcome - it will be evolution in action.
